blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Existing evaluations of text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation largely emphasize semantic fidelity and physical validity at rest, leaving interaction-time physical reliability insufficiently assessed. To address this gap, we introduce ScIntBench, a unified benchmark centered on interaction readiness: it executes prescribed manipulation actions (e.g., pushing, opening, and surface probing) in physics simulation and measures task success, capability and progress, post-interaction integrity, and dynamic plausibility. Multi-view semantic and static physical evaluations complement these metrics and help explain interaction outcomes. We systematically evaluate 12 state-of-the-art scene generation systems across 10 room types. Our results reveal that strong semantic and static physical performance does not necessarily translate into interaction readiness: a system with near-perfect static plausibility completes only 11.54% of interactions, 7 of the 12 systems produce scenes that cannot support any interaction, and even the best system succeeds in only 36.92% of prescribed tasks. These findings highlight two fundamental challenges in generating interaction-ready scenes: providing the necessary physical interaction capabilities and ensuring reliable physical behavior under active manipulation.
blocks.zh: 现有对文字条件3D室内场景生成的评价主要强调语义忠贞和休息时的物理有效性,使互动时间的物理可靠性得不到充分的评估。 为了弥补这一差距,我们引入了ScInt Bench,一个以互动准备状态为中心的统一基准:它在物理模拟中执行规定的操纵动作(如推取,开取和地表探测)并测量任务成功,能力和进展,互动后的完整性,以及动态的可信度. 多视图语义和静态物理评价补充了这些衡量标准,并有助于解释互动结果。 我们系统评估了10个房间类型的12个最先进的场景生成系统。 我们的结果显示,强健的语义和静态物理性能并不一定会转化为互动准备:一个具有近乎完美的静态性能的系统只完成11.54%的相互作用,12个系统中的7个产生无法支持任何相互作用的场景,甚至最好的系统也只成功36.92%的规定任务. 这些发现凸显出产生互动准备场景的两个根本挑战:提供必要的物理互动能力和确保在主动操纵下可靠的物理行为.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation has made substantial progress, enabling the automatic construction of increasingly complex environments from natural-language descriptions. Recent advances have expanded scene generation from data-driven generative models to LLM/VLM-based workflows, specialized agentic pipeline, and general-purpose coding agents operating through modeling tools. This evolution has broadened the goal of scene generation beyond visual content creation toward simulation-ready environments for robotics, embodied AI, and interactive applications. However, as generation systems become increasingly capable, a fundamental question remains: Are generated 3D scenes truly ready for physical interaction, and can existing evaluations reliably assess this capability?
blocks.zh: 具备文字条件的3D室内场景生成工作取得了实质性进展,使得能够从自然语言描述中自动构建日益复杂的环境. 最近的进展将场景生成范围从数据驱动的基因模型扩大到基于LLM/VLM的工作流程、专门的代理管道和通过建模工具运作的通用编码剂。 这一演化扩大了场景生成的目标,超越了视觉内容的创造,转向模拟准备的机器人环境,体现了AI,以及交互式应用. 然而,随着代际系统的能力日益增强,一个根本问题仍然是: 生成的三维场景是否真正可以进行物理互动,现有的评价能否可靠地评估这种能力?

blocks.en: Existing evaluation protocols for generated 3D scenes primarily assess semantic quality and physical plausibility at initialization. Semantic evaluation examines visual fidelity while physical evaluation measures collision, boundary violations, support correctness, and passive stability under gravity. Recent works improve semantic, structural, and agent-centric evaluation of generated 3D environments, as summarized in Tab. 1 . However, these evaluations provide limited evidence of whether generated scenes can support physical manipulation and exhibit plausible responses to active interaction.
blocks.zh: 生成的3D场景的现有评价协议主要在初始化时评估语义质量和物理可信度. 语义评价在物理评价衡量碰撞、边界侵犯、支持正确性和重力下的被动稳定性的同时,审查视觉忠诚度。 近期的作品改进了对生成的3D环境的语义,结构,以及以代理为中心的评价,如Tab所总结. 1. 然而,这些评价提供了有限的证据,说明生成的场景是否能够支持实际操纵,并显示出对积极互动的合理反应。

blocks.en: A scene that is geometrically valid and plausible at rest is not necessarily interaction-ready. For example, a refrigerator may appear correctly placed but lack the articulation required to open its door; a chair may remain stable under gravity yet behave implausibly when pushed or subjected to a load. Such failures expose two distinct limitations: interaction availability, which concerns whether a scene provides the prerequisites for an intended action, and interaction reliability, which concerns whether that action can be successfully executed with physically plausible outcomes. This motivates two research questions: (1) To what extent do conventional semantic and static evaluations characterize interaction readiness? (2) What limits interaction readiness across different scene generation paradigms: missing capabilities, unsuccessful execution, or implausible physical responses?
blocks.zh: 从几何角度讲,在休息时是可行的,但不一定可以进行互动。 例如,冰箱看起来可能放置得正确,但缺乏打开门所需的配音;椅子在重力下可能保持稳定,但在推压或承受负荷时却表现不合理。 这种失败暴露了两种不同的限制:相互作用的可用性,即某一场景是否为预期行动提供了先决条件;相互作用的可靠性,即该行动能否以实际可行的结果成功实施。 这引发了两个研究问题:(1) 常规语义和静态评价在多大程度上是互动准备的特征? (2) 何以限制不同场景生成范式的互动准备:能力缺失,执行失败,或物理反应不可信?

blocks.en: To address these limitations and advance simulation-ready scene generation, we present ScIntBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to systematically evaluate the semantic fidelity, static physical validity, and interaction-time physical reliability of generated 3D scenes across diverse generation paradigms. ScIntBench has three evaluation dimensions: a) multi-view semantic evaluation . We employ top-down render views and four corner views to better capture spatial arrangements and object relationships. b) static physical plausibility evaluation . We evaluate initialization-time physics through geometric validity checks and passive stability simulation. c) active interaction evaluation . We introduce standardized physics-based interaction tests that assess action executability, post-interaction physical integrity, and dynamic plausibility. To ensure fair comparisons, we evaluate scenes as generated, without adding missing articulations or physical properties. Together, these evaluations characterize not only the initial configuration of a generated scene but also its behavior during physical interaction, as illustrated in .
blocks.zh: 为解决这些局限性和预先模拟准备的场景生成,我们介绍了ScInt Bench,这是一个全面的基准,旨在系统地评价不同世代范式中生成的3D场景的语义忠诚性,静态物理有效性,以及交互时间物理可靠性. ScInt Bench具有三个评价层面:(a) 多视图语义评价。 我们利用自上而下的观点和四个角的观点来更好地捕捉空间安排和物体关系。 (b) 静态物理可信性评价。 我们通过几何有效性检查和被动稳定性模拟来评价初始化-时间物理学. (c) 积极互动评价。 我们引入了标准化的物理交互测试,这些测试评估动作可执行性,交互后的物理完整性,以及动态的可信度. 为确保公平比较,我们评价场景是生成的,而不增加缺失的表达或物理属性. 这些评价加在一起,不仅说明产生场景的初始配置,而且说明其在物理互动中的行为,例如:

blocks.en: We benchmark 12 state-of-the-art 3D scene generation systems across 10 room types under the same text prompts to systematically investigate their simulation readiness. Our evaluation reveals substantial interaction-time failures that are overlooked by conventional initialization-time assessments. Despite achieving strong semantic fidelity and static physical validity, several methods generate scenes that frequently fail under active interaction due to missing articulations, inconsistent physical metadata, or post-interaction physical violations. By distinguishing interaction availability from execution reliability, our analysis reveals two complementary barriers to simulation readiness: providing the necessary interaction capabilities and ensuring physically reliable behavior when those capabilities are exercised.
blocks.zh: 我们把12个最先进的三维场景生成系统作为基准,这些系统在同一个文本下覆盖10个房间类型,促使我们系统地调查它们的模拟准备状态。 我们的评价显示,互动时间方面的重大故障被传统的初始化时间评估所忽略。 尽管实现了强烈的语义忠诚度和静态物理有效性,但是由于表达缺失,物理元数据不一致,或者交互后物理侵犯,几种方法在主动互动下往往产生故障的场景. 通过区分交互可用性和执行可靠性,我们的分析揭示了模拟准备的两个互补障碍:提供必要的交互能力和确保行使这些能力时的实际可靠行为。

blocks.en: In summary, our main contributions are threefold: • We introduce ScIntBench, a unified benchmark that comprehensively evaluates interaction readiness in text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation. • We propose 4 interaction-based metrics to characterize simulation readiness beyond initialization-time validity. • We systematically benchmark 12 SOTA scene generation systems across ten room types, highlighting key challenges between static scene quality and interaction-time reliability, and identifying key failure modes that limit simulation readiness.
blocks.zh: 总而言之,我们的主要贡献有三: 我们引入了ScInt Bench,这是一个统一的基准,全面评价在文本条件3D室内场景生成中的互动准备情况。 我们提出4项基于互动的衡量标准,以描述模拟准备状态在初始化-时间有效性之后的特点。 我们系统地以12个SOTA场景生成系统为基准,涵盖10个房间类型,突出静态场景质量与互动时间可靠性之间的关键挑战,并找出限制模拟准备状态的关键故障模式.

blocks.en: Early specialized, data-driven approaches learn object distributions and spatial arrangements from large-scale indoor datasets [ 16 , 26 , 10 ] such as 3D-FRONT [ 5 ] . To enable more flexible text-conditioned generation, subsequent methods incorporate semantic representations, vision-language models (VLMs), and spatial reasoning for scene planning and layout generation [ 4 , 23 , 33 , 18 ] . More recently, agentic frameworks have extended scene synthesis through multi-step planning, tool use, and iterative refinement [ 34 , 28 , 17 ] . Additionally, general-purpose coding agents have demonstrated the ability to construct and modify 3D worlds through programmatic tools [ 13 , 36 ] . This progression has diversified scene generation paradigms, motivating unified evaluation across systems with different generation mechanisms and capabilities.
blocks.zh: 早期的专门,数据驱动的方法从大型室内数据集[16,26,10]学习物体分布和空间安排,如3D-FRONT[5]. 为了能够更灵活的文本条件生成,随后的方法包含了语义表达,视觉语言模型(VLM),以及场景规划和布局生成的空间推理[4,23,33,18]. 最近,代理框架通过多步骤规划、工具使用和迭代改进,扩展了场景合成[34、28、17]。 此外,通用编码剂已表明有能力通过方案工具[13、36]构建和修改三维世界。 这一进展使场景生成模式多样化,促使具有不同生成机制和能力的系统进行统一评价。

blocks.en: Recent research has shown a growing trend toward generating physically plausible and interactive environments for embodied AI through geometric constraints and physics-guided optimization [ 32 , 11 ] . Meanwhile, agentic frameworks further enable tool-based scene construction, executable interaction representations, and iterative refinement [ 27 , 29 , 34 , 31 , 37 , 21 ] . SAGE [ 28 ] incorporates visual and physics critics to iteratively refine scenes through simulation-based validation. SceneSmith [ 17 ] integrates articulated assets and physical property estimation to construct simulation-ready environments for downstream robotic tasks. EmbodiedSmith [ 20 ] further leverages simulated task execution feedback to jointly refine scenes and task plans. Complementary approaches explore efficient tool orchestration, code-based generation, and functional or task-driven scene refinement [ 6 , 35 , 3 , 30 ] . Despite these advances, scene refinement often focuses on initialization-time physical validity or downstream task success, rather than explicitly addressing physical violations during active interaction.
blocks.zh: 最近的研究表明,通过几何限制和物理指导优化,为体现的AI创造实际可行的互动环境的趋势正在增加[32、11]。 同时,代理框架还使基于工具的场景构建、可执行的互动表述和迭代完善[27、29、34、31、37、21]成为可能。 SAGE [28] 整合视觉和物理批评家,通过基于模拟的验证,反复完善场景. SceneSmith [17] 整合了清晰的资产和物理属性估计,为下游机器人任务构建模拟准备环境. EmformSmith [20] 进一步利用模拟任务执行反馈,共同完善场景和任务计划. 补充方法探索有效的工具编组、基于代码的生成和功能或任务驱动的场景改进[6、35、3、30]。 尽管取得了这些进展,场景的改进往往侧重于初始化-时间物理有效性或下游任务的成功,而不是在积极互动期间明确处理实际侵权行为。

blocks.en: Existing evaluation protocols primarily assess semantic fidelity, geometric consistency, and static physical plausibility through visual assessments and constraint-based checks [ 34 , 25 , 22 , 7 , 19 ] . More recent benchmarks extend the evaluation to agentic and general-purpose 3D scene construction and editing, assessing instruction satisfaction, geometric validity, and scene-state preservation [ 31 , 13 , 36 ] . SceneTeract [ 12 ] further evaluates agent-specific activity feasibility through navigability, reachability, and interaction clearance. SceneSmith [ 17 ] and EmbodiedSmith [ 20 ] further incorporate simulated robotic manipulation, but their execution-based evaluations primarily focus on downstream task success rather than scene-level physical reliability. Nevertheless, existing approaches lack a unified protocol for systematically evaluating interaction availability and physical reliability during and after active object manipulation across diverse scene generation paradigms. ScIntBench addresses this gap through multi-view semantic evaluation, static physical evaluation, and standardized simulation-based interaction tests, as summarized in Tab. 1 .
blocks.zh: 现有评价协议主要通过视觉评估和基于约束的检查来评估语义忠诚性,几何一致性和静态物理可信度[34,25,22,7,19]. 较近期的基准将评价扩大到代理和通用的三维场景建筑和编辑、评估教学满意度、几何有效性和场景状态保护[31、13、36]。 行为模式[12]通过可航行性、可达到性和互动性清除,进一步评估特定物剂活动的可行性。 SceneSmith [17] 和 EmbodySmith [20] 进一步纳入了模拟机器人操纵,但其基于执行的评价主要侧重于下游任务的成功而非场景层面的物理可靠性. 然而,现有办法缺乏一种统一的协议,无法系统地评价各种场景生成范式在积极操纵物体期间和之后的相互作用可用性和物理可靠性。 ScInt Bench通过多视图语义评价,静态物理评价,以及标准化的模拟互动测试来解决这一缺口,Tab中对此进行了总结. 1 (英语).

blocks.en: 3 ScIntBench
blocks.zh: 3 弹簧弹

blocks.en: We present ScIntBench, a unified framework for evaluating the simulation readiness of text-conditioned 3D indoor scenes. Our evaluation suite consists of comprehensive evaluation metrics, including semantic fidelity, static physical validity, and interaction-time physical reliability. An overview of our metric dimensions and performance aspects can be found in . Please see metric implementation details in our Supplementary Appendix C .

blocks.en: 3.1 Benchmark Construction
blocks.zh: 3.1 基准建设

blocks.en: ScIntBench builds on the text prompts from SceneEval [ 25 ] , covering 10 different indoor room types, and extends them with standardized interaction specifications. Each benchmark instance consists of a text description specifying object categories, attributes, and spatial relationships, together with corresponding semantic requirements and interaction tasks. To assess interaction readiness, we construct an interaction task suite based on the room descriptions. Specifically, an LLM proposes candidate interactions involving relevant object categories. Each specification defines a target object, an intended action, the required interaction capabilities, predefined success conditions, and applicable physical constraints. These interaction specifications are established independently of the generated scenes and shared across all evaluated methods, enabling consistent assessment of interaction availability and physical reliability under active manipulation. More details of construction can be found in Supplementary Appendix B .
blocks.zh: ScInt Bench基于来自SceneEval[25]的文本提示,涵盖了10种不同的室内房间类型,并扩展了它们标准化的交互规格. 每个基准实例包含一个文本描述,具体说明对象类别,属性,和空间关系,以及相应的语义要求和交互任务. 为了评估互动准备情况,我们根据会议室说明建造了一个互动任务套件。 具体而言,LLM提出了涉及相关对象类别的候选互动。 每个规格定义一个目标对象,一个预期的行动,所需的交互能力,预先定义的成功条件,以及适用的物理限制. 这些相互作用的规格独立于所产生的场景,并在所有被评价的方法中共享,以便能够在积极操纵下一致评估相互作用的可用性和物理可靠性。 有关建筑的更多详情,请参见补充附录B。

blocks.en: 3.2 Active Interaction Evaluation
blocks.zh: 3.2 积极互动评价

blocks.en: A scene that satisfies semantic and initialization-time physical constraints may still lack the capabilities required for active interaction. To assess interaction readiness, ScIntBench introduces standardized simulation-based interaction tests that evaluate both interaction availability and physical reliability. For each text prompt p p , let S m , p S_{m,p} denote the scene generated by method m m , and let 𝒯 p = { t 1 , … , t N p } \mathcal{T}_{p}=\{t_{1},\ldots,t_{N_{p}}\} denote the corresponding set of prescribed interactions, where N p N_{p} is the number of interaction tasks associated with prompt p p . This set of interactions is shared across all evaluated methods. For each interaction, we first verify the required target object and native physical capabilities, then execute supported actions in a physics simulator. We evaluate the outcomes using four complementary metrics.

blocks.en: ISR measures the proportion of interactions in 𝒯 ​ p \mathcal{T}p whose predefined goals are achieved in the generated scene S ​ m , p S{m,p} . Each action is assigned a binary success outcome based on simulator-observable state and action-specific success criteria. Unresolved controller or simulation failures are flagged separately rather than attributed to the generated scene.

blocks.en: Binary failure outcomes may conceal differences in interaction capabilities and execution progress. To capture these distinctions, ICP adopts a six-level rubric: Target Absent (0), Target Present (2), Physically Interactable (4), Interaction Initiated (6), Substantial Progress (8), and Task Success (10). A MLLM assigns scores based on the capabilities of S m , p S_{m,p} and available execution evidence. ICP is averaged over 𝒯 p \mathcal{T}_{p} to provide a graded assessment of interaction readiness. Detailed action-specific scoring criteria are provided in the supplementary material.

blocks.en: For each executed interaction t ∈ 𝒯 p t\in\mathcal{T}_{p} , PIV measures the percentage of scene objects exhibiting physical violations following manipulation. We compare scene states before execution and after a standardized settling period, checking for unintended object displacement, new or worsened interpenetration, out-of-bound placements, and loss of required support relationships. An object is counted as violated if any of these conditions occurs. Intended object motion alone is not considered a violation. Lower PIV indicates better post-interaction physical integrity.
blocks.zh: 对于每个已执行的交互 t QQ T t\in\ mathcal{ T\\p}, PIV 测量在操纵后显示物理侵犯的场景对象的百分比 。 我们比较了执行前的场景状态和标准化的定居期之后的场景状态,检查意外的物体迁移、新的或恶化的渗透、出行的安置,以及丧失必要的支助关系。 如果发生上述任何情况,物体即视为侵犯。 仅凭预定物体运动不被视为违反规定。 下PIV显示接触后身体完整性较好.

blocks.en: For each executed interaction t ∈ 𝒯 p t\in\mathcal{T}_{p} , DP provides a complementary perceptual assessment of physical behavior during interaction. Given rendered interaction videos, a MLLM evaluates observable physical behaviors, including motion naturalness, contact behavior, gravity, support, friction, and articulation consistency on a 0-10 scale. The scoring rubric distinguishes observable physical violations from insufficient visual evidence. Task failure alone does not imply physically implausible motion. Detailed scoring criteria are provided in the supplementary material.
blocks.zh: 对于每个已执行的交互 t QQ T t\in\ mathcal{ T\\p}, DP 提供了对交互过程中的物理行为的补充性认知评估. 鉴于互动视频的制作,一个MLLM以0-10尺度评价可观察到的物理行为,包括运动自然性,接触行为,重力,支持,摩擦,以及表达一致性. 分数分数区分了可观察到的人身侵犯和视觉证据不足。 单是任务失败并不意味着物理上不可能的运动。 补充材料中规定了详细的评分标准。

blocks.en: 3.3 Semantic and Static Physical Evaluation
blocks.zh: 3.3 语义和静态物理评价

blocks.en: To complement the evaluation of interaction readiness, we also evaluate semantic quality and static physical validity by adapting existing evaluation protocols with several modifications.
blocks.zh: 为了补充对互动准备状态的评价,我们还通过修改现有评价协议,对语义质量和静态物理有效性进行评估,并进行若干修改。

blocks.en: To evaluate visual and semantic fidelity, we adopt a standardized five-view rendering protocol consisting of one top-down view and four complementary corner views. The top-down view captures the global scene layout, while the corner views provide additional perspectives to reduce occlusion and reveal spatial relationships that may be ambiguous from a single viewpoint. Following SceneWeaver [ 34 ] , a MLLM jointly evaluates all five views against the corresponding text prompt using four metrics: visual realism ( Real ), functionality ( Func ), layout correctness ( Lay ), and scene completeness ( Comp ).
blocks.zh: 为了评价视觉和语义上的忠诚,我们采用了标准化的五景渲染协议,包括一个自上而下的视图和四个互补的角视图. 自上而下的视图捕捉到全球场景布局,而角景则提供了额外的视角来减少遮蔽,并揭示空间关系,从单一角度可能模糊不清. 在SceneWeaver [34] 之后, MLLM 联合评价所有五种观点与相应的文本提示,使用四个度量符:视觉现实主义(Real),功能(func),布局正确性(Lay)和场景完整性(comp ).

blocks.en: We assess initialization-time physical validity through geometric check and passive stability simulation. Following prior work [ 25 , 28 ] , geometric checks examine object collisions ( COL ), support relationships ( SUP ), and out-of-bounds placements ( OB ). Passive stability ( STAB ) is evaluated by simulating the scene under gravity without active manipulation and detecting unintended object movement, loss of support, or instability. These evaluations characterize whether a generated scene is geometrically valid and physically stable at rest, providing a reference for subsequent interaction-time assessment.
blocks.zh: 我们通过几何检查和被动稳定性模拟来评估初始化-时间物理有效性. 在先前的工作[25,28]之后,几何检查检查物体碰撞(COL),支持关系(SUP),以及出界放置(OB). 被动稳定性(STAB)是通过在重力下模拟场景来评价的,没有主动操纵和探测意外物体运动,失去支持,或不稳定. 这些评价说明生成的场景是否几何有效,在休息时身体是否稳定,为随后的互动时间评估提供了参考。

blocks.en: 3.4 Standardized Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: 3.4 标准化评价议定书

blocks.en: To ensure consistent evaluation across different scene generation methods, we adopt a unified evaluation protocol that preserves the original scene geometry, object poses, and native physical properties. Generated scenes are reconstructed in Blender [ 2 ] for standardized multi-view rendering, while geometric checks are performed on the preserved scene geometry, and simulation-based assessments are conducted in Isaac Sim [ 14 ] . Missing physical properties or articulation mechanisms are not automatically supplemented.
blocks.zh: 为确保不同场景生成方法的一致评价,我们采用统一的评价协议,保留原场景几何,物体姿势,以及原生物理属性. 生成的场景在Blender[2]中重建,用于标准化的多视图渲染,同时在保存的场景几何上进行几何检查,在Isaac Sim[14]中进行模拟评估. 缺失的物理属性或表达机制不会自动补充.

blocks.en: For each text prompt, interaction specifications and success criteria are established independently of generated scenes and shared across all evaluated methods. A calibration procedure using reference simulations validates the action executors and success conditions before evaluation. The supported interactions are then executed using standardized, task-specific manipulation procedures, with consistent execution parameters and success criteria across methods. Following each interaction, the scene is allowed to settle before assessing post-interaction physical violations. Additionally, missing target objects or required physical capabilities contribute to ISR and ICP, whereas PIV and DP are evaluated only when valid interaction evidence is available.
blocks.zh: 对于每个文本的及时性,互动规格和成功标准是独立于产生场景而确定的,并在所有评估方法中共享。 使用参考模拟的校准程序在评价前验证动作执行者和成功条件. 然后利用标准化的、针对具体任务的操作程序,以一致的执行参数和各种方法的成功标准来执行所支持的相互作用。 每次互动后,允许现场在评估互动后实际侵权行为之前就解决。 此外,缺失的目标对象或所需的物理能力有助于综合审计和比较方案,而只有在有有效互动证据时才对项目IV和DP进行评价。

blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: We evaluate 12 text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation systems spanning four paradigms: task-specific generators, including ATISS [ 16 ] , DiffuScene [ 26 ] , and InstructScene [ 10 ] ; LLM/VLM-based generators, including LayoutGPT [ 4 ] , LayoutVLM [ 23 ] , Holodeck [ 33 ] , and HSM [ 18 ] ; specialized agentic pipelines, including SceneWeaver [ 34 ] , SAGE [ 28 ] , and SceneSmith [ 17 ] ; and general-purpose coding agents, including Codex [ 15 ] and Claude Code [ 1 ] . The first group learns scene distributions from 3D-FRONT, whereas the remaining methods employ language-guided planning, hierarchical scene construction, agentic tool use, or programmatic generation.
blocks.zh: 我们评价了12个具有文字条件的3D室内场景生成系统,这些系统跨越四个范式:任务特定发电机,包括ATISS [16],DiffuScene [26],以及指令Scene [10];基于LLM/VLM的发电机,包括布局GPT [4],布局VLM [23],Holodeck [33],和HSM [18];专用代理管道,包括SceneWeaver [34],SAGE [28],和SceneSmith [17];以及通用编码代理,包括Codex [15]和Claude Code [1]. 第一组从3D-FRONT学习场景分布,其余的方法则采用语言指导规划,分级场景构造,代理工具使用,或程序生成.

blocks.en: We selected 30 prompts from SceneEval [ 25 ] , covering 10 types of indoor room (3 prompts for each type). Based on the room descriptions, we construct 203 prescribed interaction tasks. The same interaction task set is shared across all evaluated methods, yielding 2436 scene-interaction evaluation instances.
blocks.zh: 我们从SceneEval[25]中挑选了30个提示,涵盖10种室内房间(每类3个提示)。 根据房间描述,我们构建了203个规定的交互任务. 所有评估方法都共享相同的互动任务,产生了2436个场景互动评价实例。

blocks.en: We use Blender [ 2 ] for standardized five-view rendering and Isaac Sim [ 14 ] for physics-based evaluation. GPT-5.6 is employed to construct applicable interaction tasks from room descriptions and to evaluate semantic fidelity, interaction capability progress, and dynamic plausibility. Active interactions are executed using a Franka Panda robot for contact-based manipulation and a standardized force-driven probe for surface interaction tests. For method reproduction, SAGE and SceneSmith use two NVIDIA L40S GPUs, while the remaining methods use one NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU. LLM/VLM inference is performed through APIs. Further implementation details are provided in the supplementary material. Please refer to Supplementary Appendix A for more details on the baseline implementation. Please refer to Supplementary Appendix D for simulation and execution details.
blocks.zh: 我们使用Blender[2]进行标准化的五景渲染,Isaac Sim[14]进行物理评价. GPT-5.6用于从房间描述中构建适用的交互任务,并评估语义的忠诚性,交互能力的进步,以及动态的可信度. 主动相互作用使用Franka Panda机器人进行接触操纵,并使用标准化的武力驱动探测器进行表面相互作用试验。 对于方法复制,SAGE和SceneSmith使用两个NVIDIA L40S GPU,其余的方法则使用一个NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU. LLM/VLM推论通过API进行. 补充材料中提供了进一步的详细执行情况。 关于基线执行情况的更多详情,请参阅补充附录A。 关于模拟和执行细节,请参见补充附录D。

blocks.en: We report four semantic metrics (Real, Func, Lay, Comp), four static physical metrics (COL, OB, SUP, STAB), and four active interaction metrics (ISR, ICP, PIV, DP). For active evaluation, scores are first aggregated across prescribed or valid interactions within each scene and then averaged equally across scenes.
blocks.zh: 我们报告四个语义测量(Real, Func, Lay, Comp),四个静态物理测量(COL, OB, SUP, STAB),以及四个主动相互作用测量(ISR, ICP, PIV, DP). 就积极评价而言,分数首先在每一场景内通过规定或有效的互动进行汇总,然后在各场景之间平均进行。

blocks.en: 4.2 Overall Performance on ScIntBench
blocks.zh: 4.2 关于ScInt Bench的总体业绩

blocks.en: As shown in Tab. 2 , our results reveal a substantial gap between static physical validity and interaction readiness. For example, SAGE achieves strong performance in static physics, with a COL of 0.41% and STAB of 98.33%, but its ISR is only 11.54%. In contrast, Holodeck exhibits considerably worse static physical scores, but achieves a higher ISR of 17.39%. More broadly, 7 of the 12 evaluated methods cannot complete any prescribed interaction, as their scenes do not support physical simulation. As illustrated in Fig. 3 (additional results can be found in Supplementary Appendix E ), visually plausible scenes can exhibit substantially different interaction outcomes. In the refrigerator-opening task, only Claude Code achieves the required opening angle among the illustrated methods. For the table-pushing task, SAGE, SceneSmith, and Claude Code succeed, while Codex fails. These observations demonstrate that favorable initialization-time physical properties do not necessarily translate into the ability to support active manipulation.
blocks.zh: 如塔布所示. 2,我们的结果揭示了静态物理有效性与互动准备之间的巨大差距. 例如SAGE在静态物理中实现了强性能,COL为0.41%,STAB为98.33%,但其ISR仅为11.54%. 相比之下,霍洛德克显示的静态物理分数则要差得多,但达到了17.39%的更高的静态分数. 更广泛地说,12个评估方法中的7个无法完成任何规定的交互,因为它们的场景不支持物理模拟. 如图3所示(补充附录E载有额外结果),视似可信的场景可以显示截然不同的相互作用结果。 在打开冰箱的任务中,只有克劳德代码(Claude Code)在插图方法中实现了所要求的打开角度. 对于平板任务,SAGE,SceneSmith和Claude Code成功,而Codex失败. 这些观察表明,有利的初始化-时间物理属性并不一定转化为支持主动操纵的能力.

blocks.en: Interestingly, interaction readiness appears to be more closely aligned with semantic functionality than with passive physical stability. Among the 5 methods with executable interactions, the ranking by ICP exactly matches that by Func , while ISR follows a similar ordering (except for SAGE and Holodeck). This suggests that providing functionally appropriate scene content may be particularly important for enabling physical interaction.
blocks.zh: 有趣的是,互动准备似乎与语义功能比与被动的物理稳定性更紧密地配合. 在具有可执行相互作用的5种方法中,国际比较方案的排名与Func的排名完全一致,而ISR遵循类似的顺序(SAGE和Holodeck除外)。 这表明,提供适合功能的场景内容对于促成物理互动可能特别重要。

blocks.en: Furthermore, interaction success does not guarantee post-interaction physical integrity. Claude Code achieves the highest ISR but exhibits a relatively high PIV , whereas SAGE obtains the lowest PIV despite completing fewer tasks. SceneSmith achieves the highest DP , further illustrating that task completion and physical behavior capture complementary aspects of interaction readiness.
blocks.zh: 此外,互动的成功并不能保证互动后的人身安全。 Claude Code实现了最高的ISR,但显示出相对较高的PIV,而SAGE尽管完成了较少的任务,却获得了最低的PIV. SceneSmith实现了最高的DP,进一步说明了任务完成和身体行为抓住了互动准备的互补方面.

blocks.en: Another notable finding is the competitive performance of general-purpose coding agents. Claude Code leads in Real , Func , Lay , ISR , and ICP , while Codex ranks second in Func , Lay , ISR , and ICP . However, both methods obtain lower Comp scores than specialized pipelines such as SAGE and SceneSmith, suggesting that strong functional coherence does not necessarily imply richly populated scenes. Moreover, Codex and Claude Code require approximately 28 minutes per scene, substantially less than SAGE and SceneSmith. Although runtime comparisons are influenced by hardware and implementation differences, these findings highlight the potential of general-purpose coding agents for scene generation while revealing substantial opportunities to improve interaction readiness.
blocks.zh: 另一个值得注意的发现是通用编码代理商的竞争性能. Claude Code在Real、Func、Lay、ISR和ICP中领先,而Codex在Func、Lay、ISR和ICP中排名第二。 然而,这两种方法都比SAGE和SceneSmith等专业管道获得较低的comp分数,这表明强大的功能一致性并不一定意味着人口密集的场景. 此外,Codex和Claude Code要求每个场景约28分钟,大大低于SAGE和SceneSmith. 虽然运行时间比较受到硬件和执行差异的影响,但这些结论突出了场景生成的通用编码剂的潜力,同时揭示了改善互动准备状态的大量机会.

blocks.en: 4.3 Active Metrics Validation
blocks.zh: 4.3 活性计量验证

blocks.en: We further evaluate our active interaction metrics on selected reference scenes from ReplicaCAD [ 24 ] and iGibson [ 8 ] (reconstructed from real-world scans) and BEHAVIOR-1K [ 9 ] (curated interactive simulations). We evaluate matched interaction tasks using calibrated manipulation protocols and predefined success criteria. Across seven matched interaction tasks in BEHAVIOR-1K and three in iGibson, the corresponding reference scenes successfully complete all ten tasks, while each evaluated generation method achieves at most five confirmed successes across the same planned task set. These results demonstrate that our evaluation can identify interaction capability gaps between generated and reference scenes, highlighting limitations that can inform subsequent simulation-aware scene refinement. Please refer to Supplementary Sec. F.1 for more details of validation on reference scenes.
blocks.zh: 我们进一步评价我们从ReplicaCAD [24] 和 iGibson [8] (从现实世界扫描中重建) 和 BEHAVIOR-1K [9] (精确的交互式模拟) 对选定参考场景的主动互动度量。 我们利用校准的操纵协议和预先确定的成功标准来评价匹配的互动任务. 在BEHAVIOR-1K的7项互动任务和iGibson的3项互动任务中,相应的参考场景成功地完成了所有10项任务,而每个评估的生成方法最多在5项已确认的成功中完成了相同的计划任务。 这些结果表明,我们的评价可以确定生成场景与参考场景之间的相互作用能力差距,突出显示能够为随后的模拟-感知场景改进提供信息的局限性。 关于参考场景验证的详情,请参见补充Sec. F.1.

blocks.en: To assess the alignment of our MLLM-based active evaluation metrics with human judgments, we conduct a human study focusing on ICP and DP. Three annotators independently rated each of 100 interaction cases sampled from different generation methods, covering diverse action types and execution outcomes. For ICP, annotators assessed interaction capabilities and task progress using the same six-level rubric as the MLLM evaluator. For DP, annotators assessed physical plausibility from interaction videos and could indicate insufficient visual evidence. Annotators could optionally provide a rationale for their ratings. For each metric, we measured the correlation between MLLM scores and mean human ratings using Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient ( ρ \rho ) and Kendall’s τ \tau . The results are shown in Tab. 4 . Further details are provided in the Supplementary Sec. F.2 .
blocks.zh: 为了评估我们基于MLLM的积极评价指标与人类判断的一致性,我们开展了一项以比较方案和DP为重点的人类研究。 从不同生成方法抽取的100个互动案例中,有3个独立评分,涉及不同的行动类型和执行结果。 就比较方案而言,注释员使用与多边土地管理评价员相同的六级标题评估互动能力和任务进展。 对DP来说,注释者评估了互动视频的物理可信度,可能表明视觉证据不足。 注释者可以选择为其评级提供理由。 使用斯皮尔曼的阶次相关系数(ë\rho)和肯德尔的“\tau ” 来测量MLLM分数和人类平均分数之间的关联。 结果以 Tab 显示. 4. 进一步详情见补充部分F.2。

blocks.en: 4.4 Interaction Failure Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.4 相互作用失败分析

blocks.en: We further analyze the failure modes that limit the interaction readiness of generated scenes. A major limitation is the absence of required interaction capabilities. Among 2436 prescribed scene–interaction pairs, 1534 cannot be executed due to missing target objects or native physical prerequisites. For example, as shown in Fig. 3 , SAGE generates a visually plausible fridge but lacks the articulation required to open its door.
blocks.zh: 我们进一步分析限制生成场景互动准备的故障模式. 主要限制是缺乏必要的互动能力。 在规定的2436个场景-交互对中,1534个由于缺少目标物体或原生物理先决条件而无法执行. 例如,如图所示. 3,SAGE生成一个视似似冰箱,但缺乏打开门所需的配音.

blocks.en: Even when interactions can be executed, the generated scenes may fail to achieve the predefined goals. In the refrigerator-opening example, SceneSmith and Codex reach only 0.47 ∘ 0.47^{\circ} and 0.11 ∘ 0.11^{\circ} , respectively, far below the required 60 ∘ 60^{\circ} . Such cases demonstrate the importance of distinguishing interaction availability from actual task completion.
blocks.zh: 即使可以执行互动,生成的场景也可能无法实现预先设定的目标. 在打开冰箱的例子中,SceneSmith和Codex分别只达到0.47 → 0.47 → 0.47 → circ}和 0.11 → 0.11 → crc},远低于要求的60 → 60 → 6 → circ}. 此类案例表明,必须区分互动可用性和实际任务完成情况。

blocks.en: Finally, executed interactions can expose physical inconsistencies, including interpenetration, support loss, and unintended object displacement. As illustrated in (c), two non-target books originally resting on a table are displaced onto the floor following a chair-pushing interaction. These failure modes highlight the need for scene generation methods to incorporate native physical capabilities and maintain physical reliability during interaction.
blocks.zh: 最后,执行的相互作用可能暴露出物理上的不一致,包括相互渗透、支助损失和意外物体转移。 如(c)所示,原来放在一张桌子上的两本非目标书在主席与主席互动之后被移到地板上。 这些故障模式凸显出场景生成方法需要结合本土物理能力,在互动过程中保持物理可靠性.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: In this paper, we propose ScIntBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating the physical interaction plausibility of text-conditioned 3D indoor scenes across semantic quality, static physical plausibility, and active interaction behavior. By introducing four complementary interaction metrics, ScIntBench extends conventional scene evaluation beyond visual appearance and static physical validity to assess interaction capabilities and physical reliability. Our evaluation of 12 scene generation methods reveals that strong semantic and static performance does not necessarily translate into interaction readiness, with many generated scenes lacking the capabilities required for physical manipulation. We also find that general-purpose coding agents emerge as competitive alternatives to specialized scene generation pipelines, although substantial limitations in interaction success and physical reliability remain. Therefore, ScIntBench provides a standardized basis for assessing simulation readiness and informing future advances in interactive 3D scene generation.

ScInt Bench通过引入四个互补的相互作用度量衡,将常规场景评价扩展到视觉外观和静态物理有效性之外,以评估相互作用能力和物理可靠性. 我们对12个场景生成方法的评价表明,强烈的语义和静态性能并不一定转化为互动准备,许多产生的场景缺乏物理操控所需的能力. 我们还发现,一般用途编码剂是取代专门场景生成管道的竞争性替代品,尽管在互动成功和实际可靠性方面仍存在重大限制。 因此,ScInt Bent Bench为评估模拟准备状态和在交互式3D场景生成中为未来进步提供信息提供了一个标准化的基础.

blocks.en: To evaluate interaction readiness independently of scene generation methods, we construct a shared set of interaction tasks from each original text prompt. We use GPT-5.6 in a two-stage procedure. First, it identifies applicable action categories from a predefined action library and enumerates all entities explicitly mentioned in the scene description. Second, it examines each action-entity pair and determines whether the interaction is semantically applicable.

blocks.en: The current action library includes three categories: open_hinged , push_rigid , and place_push_probe , corresponding to the opening of the hinged object, the pushing of the rigid object, and surface interactions based on standardized probe. blocks.en: We evaluate generated scenes in three complementary dimensions: semantic quality, static physical plausibility, and active interaction behavior. This section provides details of implementation and scoring for the metrics introduced in the main paper. blocks.en: C.1 Semantic Quality Evaluation
blocks.zh: C.1 语义质量评价

blocks.en: Following SceneWeaver [ 34 ] , semantic quality is assessed using four criteria: realism, functionality, layout, and completeness. Each criterion is evaluated on a 0–10 scale using a MLLM-based judge.
blocks.zh: 继SceneWeaver [34] 之后,语义质量通过四个标准进行评估:现实主义,功能,布局,以及完整性. 每项标准均以0至10级标准由基于最低劳动报酬的法官评估。

blocks.en: For each generated scene, we render five standardized views using Blender: one top-down view and four corner views. Each image has a resolution of 1024 × \times 1024. The views are provided individually, together with the original scene description and structured geometric layout information.
blocks.zh: 对于每个生成的场景,我们使用Blender制作五个标准化视图:一个自上而下视图和四个角视图. 每个图像的分辨率为1024×\times 1024. 景点单独提供,同时提供原景描述和结构几何布局信息.

blocks.en: The four dimensions are defined as follows. Realism measures the visual plausibility of the generated environment. Functionality assesses whether the furnishings and spatial arrangement are suitable for the intended room activities. Layout measures the coherence of object placement and spatial organization. Completeness evaluates whether the scene contains sufficient objects and details to satisfy the text description and form a complete indoor environment. The complete scoring instructions for the MLLM are provided below:

If any critical issue is found (such as missing key objects, obvious layout errors, or unrealistic elements), the score should be significantly lowered, even if other aspects are fine. blocks.en: C.2 Static Physical Evaluation
blocks.zh: C.2 静态物理评价

blocks.en: Static physical plausibility is evaluated using four metrics: collision, out-of-bounds, support correctness (following SceneEval [ 25 ] ), and stability (following SAGE [ 28 ] ).
blocks.zh: 静态物理可信性使用四个度量标准进行评估:碰撞、边界外、支持正确性(跟踪SceneEval [25])和稳定性(跟踪SAGE [28])。

blocks.en: We use SceneEval’s [ 25 ] mesh-based collision detector, including its 5-mm contact-filtering procedure: an initially intersecting object pair is counted as colliding only if the intersection persists after the prescribed temporary separation check. This operation is performed on a detection copy and does not modify the generated scene.
blocks.zh: 我们使用SceneEval的[25]网基碰撞探测器,包括其5毫米接触-过滤程序:只有在规定的临时分离检查后,交叉点持续存在时,最初相交物体对才算碰撞。 这一操作是在检测副本上进行的,不修改生成的场景.

blocks.en: We adopt SceneEval’s [ 25 ] out-of-bounds detector, which samples points on each object’s mesh surface and casts downward rays toward the evaluation floor. An object is classified as out of bounds when fewer than 99% of its sampled points intersect the floor.
blocks.zh: 我们采用SceneEval的[25] 出界探测器,该探测器将样品点到每个物体的网状表面,并将下射线投向评估层。 当一个物体的样本点不到99%的交叉点时,该物体被归类为超出界限。

blocks.en: Following SceneEval [ 25 ] , we assess support in two stages. First, GPT-5.6 determines the expected support category of each object from multi-view visual evidence, selecting among ground, object, wall, and ceiling support. Second, We verify the corresponding geometric support relationships using an adapted ray-based contact detector.
blocks.zh: 在SceneEval [25]之后,我们分两个阶段评估支助。 首先,GPT-5.6从多视图视觉证据中确定每个对象的预期支持类别,在地面,物体,墙壁和天花板支持中选择. 第二,我们... 我们用一个经过改造的射线式接触探测器来验证相应的几何支持关系.

blocks.en: Following the stability criterion used in SAGE [ 28 ] , we simulate each scene for 120 physics steps and identify objects whose displacement exceeds 0.2 m or whose orientation change exceeds 8 ∘ 8^{\circ} relative to the initial state. Our evaluation uses Isaac Sim 5.1.
blocks.zh: 按照SAGE [28] 中使用的稳定性标准,我们模拟了120个物理步骤的每个场景,并确定了相对于初始状态,其位置移位超过0.2米或方向变化超过8 ∘ 8^{\circ}的物体. 我们的评价使用艾萨克・西姆・5.1。

blocks.en: The Interaction Success Rate measures the proportion of prescribed tasks that satisfy their predefined success conditions under the standardized interaction protocol. A task is considered successful only when its numerical success criteria are met. If the generated scene lacks the required target object or native physical prerequisites, the corresponding task is counted as unsuccessful.

blocks.en: Interaction Capability Progress provides a more fine-grained assessment of interaction readiness than binary success. We use a six-level ordinal rubric to distinguish target availability, physical interaction capability, execution progress, and successful task completion.

blocks.en: ICP Rubric Score Guidelines For the intended interaction action: • Score 10: Task Success. The interaction reaches the predefined success state. • Score 8: Substantial Progress. The interaction produces substantial and physically correct progress toward the intended outcome, but does not reach the predefined success state. • Score 6: Interaction Initiated. The intended interaction can be physically initiated and produces a valid response, but the execution fails before making substantial progress toward the predefined success state. • Score 4: Physically Interactable. The interaction target contains the required physical properties or mechanisms, such as valid collision geometry, joints, or articulation, such that the intended action is physically possible. • Score 2: Target Present. The required interaction target is present in the scene, but does not provide the physical structure or properties required for the intended action. • Score 0: Target Absent. The required interaction target is absent from the scene.

blocks.en: Post-Interaction Physical Violation measures newly introduced or worsened physical inconsistencies observed after an executed interaction. We compare the initial scene state with the state obtained after execution. We consider violations including object interpenetration, out-of-bounds conditions, unintended displacements, and loss of required support relationships. blocks.en: C.6 Dynamic Plausibility (DP)
blocks.zh: C.6 动态挥发性(DP)

blocks.en: Dynamic Plausibility evaluates whether the observed physical behavior of a scene is consistent with plausible interaction dynamics. For each executed interaction, we record target-focused and overview observations that cover the interaction progress and the post-interaction settling period. The MLLM evaluates the visual evidence from action render video frames using a fixed 0–10 scoring rubric.
blocks.zh: 动态可视性评价一个场景所观察到的物理行为是否与可能的互动动态一致. 对于每次执行的互动,我们记录以目标为重点的概览观察,涵盖互动进展和互动后结算期。 MLLM使用固定的0–10分号来评价从动作中获取的视觉证据,制作视频帧.

blocks.en:
Dynamic Plausibility Scoring Prompt Task You are given frames from an interaction video recorded in a physics simulator, the intended action, and its execution protocol. Evaluate Dynamic Plausibility (DP): ”How physically plausible are the observed scene-object behaviors throughout
the interaction?” Be a strict, evidence-grounded evaluator. High scores must be earned by visible physical behavior. Physical Criteria 1. Motion and Causality. Assess whether object motion follows contact or applied forces, with plausible acceleration, inertia, and stopping. Identify unexplained motion, discontinuities, or violations of stated constraints. Smooth motion alone does not imply correct causality. 2. Contact and Collision. Examine contact interactions across frames. Identify interpenetration, clipping, pass-through, chattering, unrealistic impacts, or missing physical coupling. Occluded contacts are unverified, and visual artifacts alone do not establish collisions. 3. Gravity and Support. Evaluate falling, settling, tipping, and support transitions, including non-target objects. A single significant violation matters. Physically coherent falling or damage is not inherently a violation; assess the underlying physical behavior. 4. Friction and Sliding. Evaluate resting, sliding onset, sustained motion, and deceleration against applied forces. Avoid inferring exact physical parameters or inventing hidden constraints to explain unexpected motion. Acknowledge insufficient evidence. 5. Rigidity and Articulation. Assess rigid-body integrity, attachments, hinge axes, and joint motion. Identify unintended detachment, deformation, pivot changes, or penetration. Respect stated rigid-body approximations. Score Guidelines • High Plausibility (8-10): Critical interaction phases are clearly observed and physically coherent, with no moderate or major violations. Minor defects or noncritical uncertainty may remain. A score of 10 requires clear positive evidence of physical plausibility. • Moderate Plausibility (4-7): The interaction remains broadly understandable but contains minor to moderate physical inconsistencies or partially observed critical phases. Scores decrease with the severity, frequency, and extent of inconsistencies. Missing evidence should not be treated as a physical violation. • Low Plausibility (0-3): Clear major physical violations undermine the interaction, ranging from isolated major failures (3) to pervasive physical incoherence (0). A single major violation limits the score to 3 or below. Missing targets and task failures do not justify a score of 0. Input Format The input will be a {action} and {rendered_video_frames}. blocks.en: Gravity and Support. Evaluate falling, settling, tipping, and support transitions, including non-target objects. A single significant violation matters. Physically coherent falling or damage is not inherently a violation; assess the underlying physical behavior.
blocks.zh: 引力与支撑. 评价掉落、沉淀、倾斜和支持过渡,包括非目标对象。 一起重大违规事件 身体连续下降或损害本质上不是侵权行为;评估潜在的身体行为。

blocks.en: Friction and Sliding. Evaluate resting, sliding onset, sustained motion, and deceleration against applied forces. Avoid inferring exact physical parameters or inventing hidden constraints to explain unexpected motion. Acknowledge insufficient evidence.
blocks.zh: 滑动和滑动。 评估休息、滑动、持续运动和对应用部队减速。 避免推断准确的物理参数或发明隐藏的制约来解释意想不到的运动. 承认证据不足。

blocks.en: Rigidity and Articulation. Assess rigid-body integrity, attachments, hinge axes, and joint motion. Identify unintended detachment, deformation, pivot changes, or penetration. Respect stated rigid-body approximations.
blocks.zh: 严与辩. 评估刚性身体完整性、附件、轴和联合运动。 确定意外的分离、变形、转轴变化或渗透。 尊重说明的刚性身体近似。

blocks.en: High Plausibility (8-10): Critical interaction phases are clearly observed and physically coherent, with no moderate or major violations. Minor defects or noncritical uncertainty may remain. A score of 10 requires clear positive evidence of physical plausibility.
blocks.zh: 高可见度(8-10):关键互动阶段得到清晰的观察和物理上的一致性,没有中度或重大违规行为. 小缺陷或非关键不确定性可能依然存在。 得分10要求有明确的正面证据来证明物理上的合理性.

blocks.en: Moderate Plausibility (4-7): The interaction remains broadly understandable but contains minor to moderate physical inconsistencies or partially observed critical phases. Scores decrease with the severity, frequency, and extent of inconsistencies. Missing evidence should not be treated as a physical violation.
blocks.zh: 中度挥发性( 4-7 ): 互动仍然大致可以理解,但包含轻微到轻微的物理不一致或部分观察到的关键阶段。 得分随不一致的严重程度、频率和程度而减少。 缺失的证据不应作为实际侵权行为处理。

blocks.en: Low Plausibility (0-3): Clear major physical violations undermine the interaction, ranging from isolated major failures (3) to pervasive physical incoherence (0). A single major violation limits the score to 3 or below. Missing targets and task failures do not justify a score of 0.
blocks.zh: 低频( 0-3) : 明显的重大人身侵犯行为破坏了互动,从孤立的重大失败(3)到普遍存在的人身不连贯(0)。 一次重大违规将得分限制在3或以下. 目标缺失和任务失败不能证明得分为0。

blocks.en: During the judgment, task failure does not automatically imply low dynamic plausibility: an interaction may fail to reach its target while exhibiting physically reasonable behavior. Conversely, successful task completion does not guarantee physical plausibility if visible violations occur.
blocks.zh: 在判断期间,任务失败并不自动意味着低动态的可信度:一种相互作用可能无法达到目标,同时表现出物理上合理的行为. 反之,成功完成任务并不能保证发生明显侵权行为时确实可信。

blocks.en: C.7 Metric Aggregation and Evaluation Coverage
blocks.zh: C.7 计量综合和评价覆盖率

blocks.en: For each scene, the interaction-level scores are aggregated over the corresponding shared task set. ISR and ICP account for the prescribed interactions, including cases in which the target object or required native capability is missing. PIV and DP are computed conditionally on valid executed interactions, and their reported averages are therefore accompanied by evaluation coverage.
blocks.zh: 对于每个场景,互动级的分数被汇总到相应的共享任务集上. ISR和ICP说明规定的相互作用,包括缺少目标对象或所需本土能力的情况。 PIV和DP的计算是有条件的,以有效的执行互动为基础,因此,它们报告的平均数附有评价范围。

blocks.en: Across the 30 scene descriptions and 12 generation methods, ScIntBench evaluates 2436 prescribed method–interaction pairs. Of these, 902 interactions are executed with valid physical evidence, while 1534 are classified as unsupported by the generated scene.
blocks.zh: 在30个场景描述和12个生成方法中,ScInt Bench评价了2436个规定的方法-交互对. 其中,902次交互都是用有效的物证执行的,而1534次被归类为被生成的场景所不支持.

blocks.en: Appendix D Simulation and Execution Protocol
blocks.zh: 附录D 模拟和执行议定书

blocks.en: D.1 Simulation Environment
blocks.zh: D.1 模拟环境

blocks.en: We conduct all interaction and physical simulation in NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.1 [ 14 ] . Each generated scene is converted into a unified representation that preserves its original geometry, object identities, and spatial arrangements. Native physical properties, including rigid-body states, collision shapes, masses, friction, and articulation constraints, are recovered from the original scene assets and their associated loading procedures.
blocks.zh: 我们用NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.1 [14] 进行所有的交互和物理模拟. 每一个生成的场景被转换为统一代表,保留其原始几何,物体身份,和空间安排. 原生的物理特性,包括刚性体态、碰撞形状、质量、摩擦和拼接约束,从原始场景资产及其相关装载程序中回收。

blocks.en: D.2 Interaction Execution and Configurations
blocks.zh: D.2 互动执行和配置

blocks.en: We evaluate three interaction families: open_hinged , push_rigid , and place_push_probe . For hinged opening and rigid pushing, we use a Franka Panda manipulator available in Isaac Sim to interact with target objects through physical contact. For surface probing, we use a standardized rigid probe with prescribed physical properties and an external force schedule.
blocks.zh: 我们评价三个互动家庭:开放的-hinged,push_rigid,以及放置的-push_probe. 对于链式开口和刚性推力,我们使用Isaac Sim可用的Franka Panda操纵器,通过物理接触与目标物体相互作用. 对于地表探测,我们使用标准刚性探测器,具有规定的物理性质和外部力量时间表.

blocks.en: D.3 Execution Protocol
blocks.zh: D.3 执行议定书

blocks.en: Before the interaction execution, we first calibrate and validate the robot execution policies on positive-control scenes (as shown in Fig. 5 ), verifying that they can successfully complete the prescribed interactions. We then apply the validated policies to generated scenes, performing target-specific setup, including object binding, contact geometry checks, and robot placement when applicable. This procedure helps distinguish failures arising from the generated scenes’ physical properties from those caused by the robot controller. Throughout evaluation, we preserve the generated scenes’ native physical properties and the predefined success criteria.
blocks.zh: 在交互执行之前,我们首先在正控场景上校准和验证机器人执行政策(如图5所示),验证它们能够成功完成规定的交互. 然后,我们将经过验证的政策应用于生成场景,进行特定目标设置,包括对象绑定,联系几何检查,以及适用时的机器人放置. 这一程序有助于区分产生场景的物理特性引起的故障和机器人控制器造成的故障。 整个评估过程中,我们保留了产生的场景的原生物理特性和预先确定的成功标准。

blocks.en: Appendix F Active Metrics Validation
blocks.zh: 附录F 活性计量验证

blocks.en: F.1 Validation on Reference Scenes
blocks.zh: F.1 参考情景验证

blocks.en: Table 7 reports the comparison between selected interactive reference scenes and scenes generated by five methods. We select rooms or regions from BEHAVIOR-1K [ 9 ] , ReplicaCAD [ 24 ] , and iGibson [ 8 ] based on their similarity to the input scene descriptions and the presence of relevant interaction targets. We evaluate matched tasks using fixed task-specific protocols and success criteria. The comparison includes seven planned interaction tasks in BEHAVIOR-1K, three in ReplicaCAD, and three in iGibson, with results aggregated across task types within each reference set.
blocks.zh: 表7报告选定互动参考场景与五种方法产生的场景的比较。 我们从BEHAVIOR-1K [9], ReplicaCAD [24],以及iGibson [8] 中根据它们与输入场景描述的相似性和相关交互目标的存在来选择房间或区域. 我们利用特定任务的固定规程和成功标准来评价相应的任务。 比较包括BEHAVIOR-1K的7项计划互动任务、ReplicaCAD的3项任务和iGibson的3项任务,在每个参考集内对不同任务类型的成果进行汇总。

blocks.en: F.2 Human Evaluation
blocks.zh: F.2 人类评价

blocks.en: Fig. 8 illustrates our human evaluation interface. Participants are presented with the intended action and its success criteria, followed by two interaction videos showing the target and overview perspectives. We also provide the physical properties and measurements for reference. On the right side of the interface, participants independently rate interaction capability progress (ICP) and dynamic plausibility (DP) using the same scoring rubrics as the MLLM-based evaluator in our ScIntBench. Participants may optionally provide reasons for their rating. Thus, we use these human annotations to assess the correlation of the scores given by ScIntBench metrics with human preference.
blocks.zh: 图8说明了我们的人力评价接口。 向与会者介绍了计划采取的行动及其成功标准,然后是两段互动录像,介绍目标和概况。 我们还提供物理特性和测量,以供参考。 在界面的右侧,参与者使用与我们ScInt Bench中基于MLLM的评价器相同的评分分,独立评分交互能力进度(ICP)和动态可信度(DP). 参与者可以选择提供评分的理由. 因此,我们用这些人类说明来评估ScInt Bench 度量衡给定的分数与人类偏好的相关性.

blocks.en: Figure 8 : Human evaluation interface for active metrics validation. Participants inspect synchronized target and overview videos, the intended action, and supporting physical measurements. They independently assess interaction capability and progress (ICP) using a six-level rubric and dynamic plausibility (DP) on a 0–10 scale.
blocks.zh: 图8:主动度量衡验证的人类评价接口. 参与者检查同步的目标视频和概览视频、计划采取的行动和支持物理测量。 它们独立地评估互动能力和进展,在0-10尺度上使用六级标题和动态可信度。
